title: Moles of carbon dioxide
change: New substance (CO₂, 4.40 g, 44.0 g/mol), new context (fermentation vessel); the third distractor now targets an incomplete formula-mass sum instead of a doubled molar mass.

title: Mass of sodium chloride needed
change: Task shape reversed (moles to mass instead of mass to moles); new substance, numbers and a lab-prep context.

title: Mass from particle count
change: Two-step task shape (particles → moles → grams) using Avogadro's number; new species (NH₃) and context; distractors target skipped steps and inversion.

title: Moles of ethanol
change: Different substance (ethanol), different numbers and a different distractor family (missing atom replaces the halved molar mass).

title: Moles of aluminum atoms
change: Monatomic element instead of a compound; new context; distractors use atomic-number confusion and multiplication.

title: Moles of oxygen gas
change: Diatomic gas; the key error is treating O₂ as atomic O; new numbers and context.

title: Configuration of Mn²⁺
change: Different ion (Mn2+, half-filled 3d result) and context; same removal-order misconception targets.

title: Configuration of Co³⁺
change: Higher charge (3+) and a different metal (Co); context is a coordination compound; distractors include the under-ionized Co2+ configuration.

title: Configuration of Ti²⁺
change: Early-d metal (Ti2+) where the correct answer keeps electrons in 3d; new distractor (4s electrons moved into 3d).

title: PES: six-peak atom
change: Larger spectrum (six peaks, Period 4), new element and phrasing; distractors add a peak-count-as-Z error and an assumed-full-subshell error.

title: PES: five-peak atom
change: Different element and peak pattern (p-block, ending in 3p³); different distractor mix (valence-only matching).

title: PES: predicting the atom
change: Reversed task shape (given ratio, choose the element that would produce it) with a Period 2 atom; distractors rely on matching only the valence pattern.

title: Ionization energy: Be and B
change: Different period and pair (Be/B, period 2) with the same subshell-energy explanation; distractors replace the radius duplicate with a core-shielding error.

title: Ionization energy: Zn and Ga
change: Period 4 pair (Zn/Ga) in the same subshell-energy pattern; different distractors (principal-shell error, wrong d-subshell occupancy).

title: Ionization energy: N and O
change: Different anomaly (paired-electron repulsion, N/O) from the seed's subshell-energy explanation; same misconception targets (nuclear charge only, reversed radius). Reviewer should confirm pairing repulsion is acceptable under CED 1.7 scope (qualitative Coulombic reasoning).

title: Planar carbonyl molecule
change: New species (CH₂O, PH₃, SO₂, SiH₄), new framing as Lewis diagrams; adds a double-bond-as-one-region test and an electron-domain-vs-molecular-geometry distractor.

title: Nitrate ion shape
change: Different species (an ion), shape is named directly rather than chosen from a formula list; targets double-bond-as-one-region and nitrate/nitrite confusion.

title: Flat 120 degree ion
change: Ion with resonance, three-atom-bonded distractors from different families (pyramidal, T-shaped, bent), stem specifies 120° and three identical atoms.

title: Greatest ionic character
change: New elements (Na, H, S, N, Cl, O), no fluorine; same task but distractors target add-instead-of-subtract, highest-EN-atom, and metal-excluded errors.

title: Rank ionic character
change: Task shape changed to ranking four bonds in increasing order; different atoms (K, Si, P, H, S, Br, Cl); errors are reversed direction, sum, and H-as-metal.

title: Bond with most ionic character
change: Different atoms; correct bond is not the one with an extreme atom (not the metal with lowest EN and not the F-containing bond), so three attractive heuristics all fail.

title: Beyond the octet
change: New species (XeF₂, PCl₃, BF₃, HCN); includes electron-deficient and multiple-bond distractors in place of CO₂ and SiCl₄.

title: Electrons around iodine
change: Task shape changed from choosing a species to counting electrons around a named central atom (IF₅, period 5).

title: Ion with expanded shell
change: Ion-based task with a halogen central atom; distractors are resonance, period-3 and ion-charge errors.

title: Central oxygen in ozone
change: Different species (ozone), central rather than terminal atom, and the three wrong values come from different formal-charge counting errors.

title: Nitrogen in nitrate
change: Different species and atom (central N in an ion with no lone pairs); distractors include ion-charge-as-formal-charge.

title: Carbon in carbon monoxide
change: Diatomic with a triple bond, formal charge on carbon; sign and neutral-molecule traps.

title: Shape of XeF₄
change: New species (XeF₄, 6 domains, two lone pairs); distractors target counting one lone pair instead of two and a tetrahedral-by-default shape.

title: Shape of BrF₃
change: New species (BrF₃, five domains with two lone pairs, T-shaped); wrong answers mix different lone-pair counts.

title: Identify molecule from shape
change: Reverse task shape: given EDG domain count and shape, identify the formula; new species set (IF₅, XeF₄, SF₆, PCl₅).

title: He and Kr kinetic energy
change: Seed asked for the fastest of four gases at one temperature. Variant uses two noble gases at 298 K and asks for a statement pairing KE and speed, adding the KE-versus-speed conflation targets. Substances, temperature, and task shape (statement comparison) all changed.

title: Ranking gas speeds at 400 K
change: Seed picked the single fastest gas among noble gases. Variant uses Ne/N2/Cl2 (mixed monatomic and diatomic), different temperature, and a full ranking task shape, which adds the equal-speed and atom-count misconceptions.

title: H₂ versus O₂ speed ratio
change: Seed was a qualitative who-is-fastest question. Variant is a quantitative speed-ratio question with H2 and O2 at 300 K, requiring KE = 1/2 mv^2 manipulation (the CED equation), a different task shape and substances.

title: Absorbance after fourfold dilution
change: Seed halved the concentration of a 0.60 absorbance solution. Variant uses CuSO4, starting absorbance 0.80, and a fourfold dilution, so the proportional-reasoning factor is different and the 'it was only halved' distractor replaces the seed's 'quartered' one.

title: Absorbance in a longer cell
change: Seed varied concentration (halved) at fixed path length. Variant holds concentration fixed and doubles the path length (1.0 cm to 2.0 cm), using a different dye and starting absorbance of 0.45, so the controlled variable and the proportional factor both change.

title: Unknown concentration from absorbance
change: Seed predicted absorbance after a concentration change. Variant reverses the direction: given a standard (0.020 M, A = 0.30) and an unknown (A = 0.75), find the unknown concentration. New numbers, context (standard versus unknown), and task shape.

title: Maximizing dissolved oxygen
change: Seed asked which T/P change most increases solubility of a nonreactive gas with options listed as change phrases. Variant uses O2 in a sealed vessel and absolute conditions (5 vs 40 C, 0.5 vs 3.0 atm) rather than described changes, with distractor logic spanning each single and double reversal.

title: Dissolved oxygen in lake water
change: Seed combined T and P changes as four paired options. Variant is a single-change environmental scenario (lake water, dissolved O2) with the question reversed to 'which decreases', and distractors adding a pressure reversal, a temperature reversal and a rate-versus-extent error.

title: CO₂ solubility on heating
change: Seed ranked four T/P combination changes. Variant isolates a single temperature change at held pressure for CO2/water and asks for amount plus reason, so the choices test rate-versus-equilibrium, ignoring temperature, and a right-answer/wrong-reason mechanism.

title: Gas volume after compression
change: Seed: 2.0 L, 1.0 atm to 4.0 atm. Variant: 6.0 L, 3.0 atm to 9.0 atm; initial pressure is no longer 1.0 atm, so the P1 factor in P1V1/P2 matters. Same Boyle relationship with new numbers.

title: Syringe plunger withdrawn
change: Seed compressed a gas. Variant expands air in a syringe (pressure falls from 2.0 to 0.50 atm), uses mL, different starting values, and a lab-style context, so the correct direction of change is reversed.

title: Pressure after isothermal compression
change: Seed solved for the final volume given a pressure change. Variant solves for the final pressure given a volume change (5.0 L to 2.0 L), a different unknown and numbers, with the distractors built from the corresponding errors.

title: Boiling points of similar-mass liquids
change: Seed compared CH4, CH3Cl, CH3OH, C2H6. Variant uses ethanol, dimethyl ether, propane and fluoroethane (all of similar molar mass, 44-48 g/mol), which removes the molar-mass shortcut and adds the H-on-carbon-with-F error.

title: Why HF boils above HCl
change: Seed asked for the highest boiling point among four formulas. Variant is an explanation question (HF versus HCl) rather than a ranking, using different substances and testing intra- versus intermolecular forces, molar-mass shortcut and polarity classification.

title: Highest boiling hydride or gas
change: Seed compared small carbon compounds. Variant compares main-group hydrides and N2 (NH3, PH3, GeH4, N2), so the trap is molar mass versus hydrogen bonding, with different substances and different error patterns (H on P, N without H).

title: Ethanol versus dimethyl ether
change: Isomer pair of different compounds (ethanol/dimethyl ether), equal molar mass; seed used CH3F vs CH3OH with similar molar mass. Distractors target size, polarity and H-donor misconceptions.

title: Why water boils higher than H2S
change: Different substances (H2O vs H2S) in which the correct-boiling-point molecule has the LOWER molar mass; seed compared similar-mass molecules. Adds intra/intermolecular and polarizability distractors.

title: Methylamine versus ethane
change: Nitrogen-based H-bond donor (amine) versus nonpolar alkane; seed used O-H alcohol versus fluoroalkane. Different distractor set (intra/inter, trivial mass difference, C-H H-bonds).

title: Hard, nonconducting, high melting solid
change: Different property set (hard, brittle, nonconducting in both states, very high mp) leading to a network solid; seed identified a metallic solid. Distractors now target high-mp misassociations.

title: Brittle solid that conducts when molten
change: Identifies an ionic solid from conductivity-on-melting evidence with mp value; seed identified a metal from conductivity in both states and malleability.

title: Soft low-melting nonconductor
change: Molecular solid with low mp, softness and solubility in nonpolar solvent; seed identified a metallic solid. All distractor types of solid represented through different property mismatches.

title: Pressure of argon in a tank
change: New gas (Ar), n = 0.250 mol, V = 5.00 L, T = 47C; same solve-for-P task as seed with a tank context.

title: Moles of gas in a flask
change: Solves for n instead of P; new gas (N2), V = 4.00 L, P = 1.50 atm, T = 127C; distractors from inverted rearrangement and omitted R.

title: Volume of a gas sample
change: Solves for V; new gas (He), n = 0.800 mol, P = 2.50 atm, T = 25C; flexible container instead of rigid.

title: Hydrogen and carbon dioxide at one temperature
change: Different gas pair (H2/CO2, 300 K) with a wider mass gap; distractors reworded around KE-vs-speed confusion rather than copying the seed's contradictory option.

title: Doubling the Kelvin temperature
change: Same-gas temperature-change task with quantitative proportionality (T doubled) rather than comparing two gases; seed compared He and O2 at same T.

title: Helium and argon in one vessel
change: Gas mixture in one vessel with a quantitative speed ratio sqrt(M_Ar/M_He) = 3.2; seed compared separate samples qualitatively.

title: Conditions for ideal carbon dioxide
change: Choose-the-best-conditions task with temperature/pressure combinations for CO2; seed asked which set gives the greatest deviation with reasons in the options. Correct answer here is the ideal regime (high T, low P).

title: Ammonia versus methane deviation
change: Compares two real gases (NH3/CH4) at moderate conditions focusing on the attraction effect on measured pressure; seed asked for T/P conditions of greatest deviation.

title: Cooling nitrogen toward condensation
change: Rigid-flask cooling scenario with N2 near its boiling point and measured-vs-ideal pressure; seed asked a general which-conditions-and-why question.

title: Warm soda goes flat
change: Seed: generic O₂ in water. Variant: CO₂ in two open soda bottles at 4 °C vs 22 °C; everyday context; distractors re-worded around soda.

title: River oxygen downstream
change: Seed: abstract O₂ question. Variant: field data (upstream vs downstream of a power plant, 8 °C vs 28 °C), same-air condition stated, new distractor set (particle expansion, vapor displacement, endothermic overgeneralization).

title: Polar versus tropical CO₂
change: Seed: heating water, O₂. Variant: reversed framing (why cold water holds more), CO₂ in polar vs tropical oceans, new distractors (ion-dipole misidentification, density-as-pressure, temperature-dependent polarity).

title: Dye concentration from absorbance
change: Seed: ε 1.50 x 10^3, A 0.750. Variant: dye, ε 2.40 x 10^4, A 0.360, same b = 1.00 cm; same task shape (solve for c).

title: Concentration in a longer cuvette
change: Seed: b = 1.00 cm. Variant: b = 2.00 cm, ε 8.50 x 10^2, A 0.425; the path length now matters, so distractors target ignoring or misplacing b.

title: Solve for path length
change: Seed: solve for c with b given. Variant: solve for path length b with c and ε given; new numbers and a different unknown.

title: Blue versus red laser
change: Seed: UV vs IR in general. Variant: two visible laser pointers (450 nm, 650 nm); distractors re-framed (inverse frequency, equal speed, direct wavelength proportionality).

title: X-ray versus microwave photon
change: Seed: UV vs IR. Variant: X-ray vs microwave (very different regions) with an added intensity condition; distractors target intensity-vs-photon-energy, speed-vs-wavelength and wave-size confusions.

title: Compare photon given λ and ν
change: Seed: conceptual UV vs IR. Variant: quantitative comparison where one photon is given by wavelength and the other by frequency (requires c = λν); no calculator needed.

title: Separating hexane and toluene
change: Seed: acetone/water (polar). Variant: hexane/toluene, both nonpolar; boiling-point difference tied to London dispersion forces; distractors changed (size, separatory funnel, recrystallization).

title: Pigments on chromatography paper
change: Seed: choose a technique for two miscible liquids. Variant: interpret a paper-chromatography result for two pigments and explain the movement; different task shape and distractors.

title: Filtering a copper sulfate solution
change: Seed: pick a technique for two liquids. Variant: interpret a failed filtration of an ionic solution; the species is a dissolved solid; task shape is explain-an-observation.

title: Diluting hydrochloric acid
change: Seed: 25.0 mL of 2.00 M to 200.0 mL. Variant: 10.0 mL of 6.00 M HCl to 250.0 mL in a volumetric flask; same task shape (find M2), new numbers and context.

title: Stock volume to prepare
change: Seed: find final molarity from V1 and V2. Variant: find the stock volume needed (V1) for a target solution; different unknown and distractor set (inversion, water volume, M2V2).

title: Adding water to permanganate
change: Seed: states the final total volume. Variant: gives volume of water added, so the student must compute the total (100.0 mL); distractors include volume-weighting error (simple average).
